assessment.nobel_worthiness: Detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, then the TXS 0506+056 association and the Galactic-plane signal, opened neutrino astronomy as a new observational window. The cubic-kilometre Antarctic ice detector is a bold instrument achievement, which I weigh heavily as an instrument builder; the physics is clear and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and drove the IceCube concept and Spiering was a central figure in the AMANDA-to-IceCube path and the discovery programme. Credited names support a two-person prize; other IceCube leaders and AMANDA pioneers could be argued for, and I cannot independently verify who was decisive.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is confirmed by several analyses and the source associations have grown over a decade; ANTARES and KM3NeT add context. Timing looks right, though individual source identifications are still evolving.
uncertainties: Whether credit should also reach other IceCube or AMANDA leaders is unresolved.
The flux is established but source populations remain only partly identified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, from the magic-wavelength idea to clocks at the 10^-18 level, are a transformative precision-measurement technology with uses in geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and a future redefinition of the second. Impact is broad and the idea is clean.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice scheme and demonstrated the early clocks; Ye's group drove the record-precision demonstrations and many-body clock physics. A two-person prize is a fair configuration. Others such as Takamoto and Lemonde may be argued for, which I cannot resolve here.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups have reproduced and surpassed the early results, and comparisons between clocks are routine. This is mature and likely timely. My own expertise in atomic physics is limited, so I would lean on colleagues.
uncertainties: Overlap with Ye's other candidacy (thorium clock) and with earlier frequency-comb recognition.
Possible additional contributors to early lattice-clock demonstrations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of X-ray, optical and radio afterglows established that gamma-ray bursts are at cosmological distances and solved a 30-year puzzle. This came from combining a precise X-ray satellite instrument with rapid follow-up, which is the kind of instrument-led discovery I respect.
assessment.attribution: BeppoSAX Wide Field Cameras and the Gamma-Ray Burst Monitor (Costa, Frontera) gave the arcminute localisation and X-ray afterglow; Kulkarni's group delivered redshift and radio and counterpart work. The other decisive figures, notably van Paradijs (deceased) and Piro, Djorgovski and Frail, are outside the list. Three names is plausible but contested.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many independent follow-ups, Swift and subsequent GRB-supernova and gravitational-wave links. Very mature, with the risk that this is no longer perceived as timely.
uncertainties: Credit is complicated by deceased contributors and by the optical and radio discoverers not credited here.
Whether the committee views this as already recognised through adjacent cosmology prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Predicting and observing the quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators created a new organizing principle in condensed matter, with consequences for spintronics and quantum materials. Importance is very high.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the founding theoretical proposals; Molenkamp's group did the first HgTe experimental observation following Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang. That leaves Zhang, Bernevig and the 3D topological insulator experiments (Hasan, Cava and others) outside this list, so the allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed by many groups and materials. The field is mature. This is condensed matter, and I defer to colleagues on how it should be weighed against other candidates in that area.
uncertainties: Attribution between 2D and 3D topological insulators is unresolved; Zhang's death complicates the picture.
I am outside my own expertise here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale image of M87* and later Sgr A* directly probe strong-field gravity and black-hole accretion. The global millimetre VLBI array is a remarkable instrumental and calibration achievement, and the images are of great public and scientific interest.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed imaging the shadow and Doeleman built and led the array, with Zensus an additional credited name. The work is an enormous collaboration, and it is hard to name one to three people as decisive without discounting hundreds of contributors.
assessment.maturity: Two independent targets and multiple epochs have been published; interpretation, including the polarisation and the model-dependence of mass and spin, is still being refined. Reasonable but somewhat early.
uncertainties: Collaboration size makes a fair three-person allocation hard to defend.
Model dependence of the shadow-size interpretation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene launched the field of moire quantum materials with very rapid, wide uptake. Originality and impact are high.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 experimental observations. Cao and Fatemi as first authors, and Dean and others working on related moire systems, are outside the credited names; a theory plus experiment split looks natural.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many groups, but the pairing mechanism and many correlated phases are still debated, and the field is only about eight years old. It may be premature.
uncertainties: The origin of the superconductivity is not settled.
Timing may be early compared with other candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed light below the shot-noise limit, now used in gravitational-wave detectors, is a clear case of quantum technology giving a practical improvement in measurement sensitivity. I value the detector impact.
assessment.attribution: Caves's theory of quantum-limited interferometry and Kimble's first observation of squeezing, with Schnabel's work on practical squeezed sources for GEO600 and LIGO. Four credited names, including Mavalvala, and others such as Slusher and Wu, make a three-person split disputable.
assessment.maturity: In routine use in LIGO, Virgo and GEO600 since 2010-2019, so the confirmation is strong. Recognition may be seen as partly absorbed by the 2017 gravitational-wave prize and 2012 quantum optics prize.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier Nobel recognition of related fields.
Several equally decisive experimental groups are not included.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Silicon microstrip and hybrid pixel detectors underlie vertex and tracking systems across particle physics, and their spin-offs in photon counting and imaging are widespread. As a detector builder I believe instrument breakthroughs deserve prize-level recognition.
assessment.attribution: Parker's microstrip work, Heijne's silicon-detector work at CERN and Campbell's hybrid pixel (Medipix) developments are distinct contributions; the credited set could be reasonable, but Kemmer, Hallewell and others are not on the list and the contributions are not a single discovery.
assessment.maturity: Decades of use at LEP, the LHC and in imaging prove the technology; however, recognition for instrumentation within the physics prize has been rare, so the fit is uncertain.
uncertainties: Whether a technique spanning decades and many people can be reduced to three laureates.
Prize-category fit for a detector technology.
